purpose: A modest gritty finish for the three existing animated fantasy game concept grids, retaining their cartoon proportions and readable features.

boards.title: Road Escort — grittier
boards.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather / style-transfer.
Asset type: a targeted art-direction edit of an existing ten-model Crownroad cartoon game concept grid.
Input image role: EDIT TARGET. Edit this exact board. The user requests "a bit more gritty", while retaining the approved simplified, animated cartoon game style.

Primary change: Give the models a modest, clearly visible battle-worn fantasy finish, roughly twenty percent grittier. Keep the appealing cartoon proportions, sculpted shapes, lively poses and instantly recognizable class features. Make grit through a few large intentional graphic wear marks and a more rugged material response, not extra detail density.

Targeted changes to the models:
- Slightly mute the clean jewel colors: teal becomes dusty deep teal, cream becomes warm weathered linen, burgundy becomes worn oxblood, gold becomes older antique brass. Preserve clear faction colors and color separation.
- Armor is dark satin iron with broad broken highlights, lightly tarnished trim, a few small readable chips on exposed edges and two or three broad scuff marks. Materials feel weightier and less pristine. Do not cover it in scratches or rust.
- Cloth has dusty lower hems, a few simple softened tears or patches, slightly faded painted emblems. Keep the broad simple folds and crisp readable silhouette. No fine fabric weave.
- Leather and wood have a few purposeful worn edges and rubbed areas; chunky wood planes and big structural features stay clean and readable. No noisy grain.
- Human faces become a little tougher and more determined through stronger brows, restrained cheek shading and subtle outdoor dust, still expressive adult cartoon faces. Preserve each person's identity, hairstyle and original anatomy. No photoreal skin or wrinkle texture.
- Undead bone has a lightly weathered warm-gray finish, with a little dark recess shading. Keep expressively cartoon skulls and creature faces, no gore.
- Architecture and props get restrained soot near heat sources, a few broad masonry chips, dusty feet/bases, weathered paint and slightly darker subdued moss. Keep the same simplified construction and low detail level.
- Lantern and spell glows stay readable but a little less candy-bright. Broad neutral studio light, subtly deeper form shadows, enough fill that every asset remains easy to see. The background stays light neutral.

Invariants: same exact ten subjects and cell positions, same identities, equipment, gestures, silhouette proportions, full bodies and complete props, five-column two-row landscape layout, same heading and exact readable labels and numbering. Preserve the key design choices rather than redesigning the models. Keep every model fully inside its own cell, with comfortable edge padding; adjust projecting weapon or banner tips minimally if needed. No extra props, no extra decorative fittings, no new scene/background content.
Constraints: polished stylized 3D animated fantasy game art, moderately cartoony. Only a modest gritty finish. Keep simplicity and readability. No move toward photorealism, no microtexture noise, no extensive grime layer, no overly dark rendering, no horror imagery, no thick outlines, no watermark.

Board-specific focus: show road dust on boots, canine paws, cloak hems and bridge edges; lightly worn shield paint and work-used timber. The hound retains its playful animated personality with a more alert focused expression. Preserve the exact "D — ROAD ESCORT" heading and all ten original labels.
